purpose: Faces/people captured-footage evaluation corpus for Milestone 5.5. Genuinely camera-captured scenes containing real, named human faces at meaningful scale, native landscape orientation, never used for training, checkpoint selection or hyperparameter tuning.
why_this_exists: Milestone 5 could not measure faces: the only permissively licensed face footage found at sufficient resolution was 9:16 vertical, and fitting it to the 2560x1440 HR master required a 2.11x synthetic upscale that made the 'ground truth' itself interpolated. This corpus instead requires camera-native landscape footage whose active picture (post letterbox/pillarbox removal) is independently verified to be at least 2560x1440, so the master is a real optical crop, never a synthetic upscale.
source: Wikimedia Commons (NASA-catalogued video, all works of the U.S. federal government)
licence_policy: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain only, read from each file's own imageinfo via the Commons API (see tools/fetch-captured.py). Sources are NOT redistributed: the fetcher pins URL and SHA-256 and a clone re-fetches.
independence: Fully disjoint from data/captured/manifest.json (the frozen Milestone 5 test set, digest eadceb4dcf76e5c35057766ab82c639012c8ede7997c592e313988cdf6c56dca) and from data/captured-train/manifest.json (the GOP-aware training corpus): no shared clip id, no shared upload, no shared source SHA-256, and no overlap in subject, uploader or collection. The frozen and training corpora are aerial drone footage, street/urban scenes, trains and nature b-roll from independent Commons uploaders (Drozwik Drones, Ride With R, Hofer, various rail videographers, etc.) with zero people at meaningful facial scale. This corpus is exclusively NASA-catalogued Artemis II/III video (ceremonies, mission-control interviews, a launch-director speech, a crew homecoming and a crew-announcement press event), catalogued by NASA Headquarters, Johnson Space Center and Kennedy Space Center respectively - a disjoint medium, collection and set of uploaders/subjects.
active_area_requirement: Every clip's active picture (source dimensions minus any detected letterbox/pillarbox bars) must be >= 2560x1440. Verified per-clip with `ffmpeg -vf cropdetect=limit=24:round=2:reset=0` over the 24 frames at start_seconds, cross-checked by extracting and visually inspecting the actual frame. See each clip's activeAreaCrop/activeAreaWidth/activeAreaHeight.
alignment_verification: tools/captured-align.py run at h264_high, h264_typical and h264_poor (see results/captured-faces-alignment-*.json and results/captured-faces-summary.json). Passes 0-problem at h264_high for all 8 clips. Under heavier compression the off-by-one margin drops below the tool's 1.0 dB bar for the 2 lowest-motion clips (near-static podium speakers: announcement-another-step-toward-one-of, speech-artemis-ii-live-launch-coverage-c) while the shuffle-collapse control stays strongly positive throughout (>=6.9 dB) - a low-motion artifact, not a geometry defect. The other 6 higher-motion clips keep >=1.8 dB margins even at h264_poor.

excluded_candidates.title: 9:16 vertical face footage considered in Milestone 5 (unnamed, see data/captured/manifest.json known_gaps)
excluded_candidates.reason: Active picture only 1214px wide; fitting to the 2560x1440 HR master required a 2.11x synthetic upscale, making the ground truth interpolated rather than optically captured. Not re-considered here.

excluded_candidates.title: File:Another step toward one of the most complex spaceflight missions in history...(Artemis III Announcement Recap).webm, segment near t=63s
excluded_candidates.reason: That specific segment is an animated Moon-phase graphic explicitly captioned 'Animation' in the source file. Excluded by choosing start_seconds=82.0, a different, verified-optical segment of the same file (a real press-conference speaker), instead of discarding the whole source.

scope_limitation: All 8 clips are NASA/Artemis-program video from 2025-2026, so subjects skew toward NASA personnel and astronauts in professional/ceremonial dress rather than a demographically or occupationally general population; this supports a claim about that population, not a general-purpose faces benchmark.
